# pi-devguard

> A read-only runner that invokes six sibling Pi measurement tools as subprocesses and
> reports one verdict per tool. It never says "safe". A clean run is not a pass.

## One-line answers

- What is this? One command that runs six sibling tools and prints one verdict each,
  always next to the exit code it read.
- Does it import the other tools? **No.** Every tool is a subprocess through its own CLI.
- Does it add its own verdict? **No.** It repeats the tool's exit code and labels it.
- Does it say anything is safe? **No.** There is no verdict word for it.
- Is a clean run a pass? **No.** `nothing-found` is a fact about the input, not the system.
- Is a non-zero exit a failure? **Not automatically.** For these tools `1` often means
  "I found something".
- Does it touch the network by default? **No.** Offline commands are the default; `--live`
  reads public endpoints only.
- What are the tools? `scanner` (SDK anti-patterns), `simulator` (Testnet contract calls),
  `registry` (API drift), `integrity` (event coverage), `chaos` (failure shapes),
  `proofkit` (portable proof packs).
- What are the verdicts? `measured` · `nothing-found` · `undetermined`. Exactly three.
- What is the runner's own exit code? `0` when every tool reached a verdict, `2` when one
  could not. It never exits `1`.
- How do I check it? `node guard.mjs` (offline), `node guard.mjs --live` (live),
  `node test/run.mjs` (offline invariants).

## Commands (zero-dependency)

```
node guard.mjs                    # offline reading for every tool
node guard.mjs --live             # live reading where a tool has one
node guard.mjs --tool <id>        # one tool
node guard.mjs --scan-dir DIR     # the directory the scanner reads
node guard.mjs --json             # machine-readable
node guard.mjs --html [FILE]      # self-contained HTML report
node guard.mjs --verbose          # include raw tool output
node guard.mjs --tools            # the tool registry
node guard.mjs --verdicts         # the verdict vocabulary and exit maps
node guard.mjs --sources          # the sibling tools, by purpose
node guard.mjs --boundaries       # every non-claim
node test/run.mjs                 # offline invariants
```

## Claim kinds

Every statement is exactly one of: `measured` · `documented` · `external` · `not-claimed`.

## Never claimed

Safety, completeness of the tool set, adoption, endorsement, obligation, or that a clean
run is a pass. No prediction about any subject's behaviour.

## Scope

Read-only, unofficial. Not affiliated with Pi Network. A result describes a tool's run,
not the system the tool was pointed at.
